title: The VFX Supervisor Daily
description: What the day's VFX news means, in a few lines, with a link to every story.

items.title: #20: Nolan's single-vendor Odyssey and a pricey Potter series shape how to pitch
items.summary: The Odyssey kept its shot count under 500 by building monsters for real first, a model for lean bids.
items.content_html:
The Odyssey kept its shot count under 500 by building monsters for real first, a model for lean bids. HBO's Harry Potter series budget suggests demand for creature and environment work. Worth watching how AI cost talk reaches clients.

Practical first, fewer shots

Practical-first plates kept The Odyssey's shot count low, yet the Cyclops still needed heavy augmentation. Bids for similar work should price plate clean-up and editorial prep, not just final shot count. Pipeline write-ups are also useful references for creature and compositing budgets.

  • Andrew Jackson & DNEG Embark on a Different Journey with 'The Odyssey' · Animation World Network Shows a sole-vendor DNEG job where a low shot count hid 260,000 frames of augmentation: price the prep, not just the count
  • Godzilla Minus Zero publishes its VFX breakdown and shows its pipeline · foro3d.com A pipeline breakdown on a kaiju made with limited resources is a usable reference for tight-budget creature bids
  • Moana: Weta FX Brings Te K? and Te Fiti to Life in the Epic Third Act · artofvfx.com Credits Weta FX with the prologue, storm and third act sequences on Moana, a guide to how big sequences get split

Update: Nuke Stage and the Mac

  • Foundry’s Nuke Stage now supports macOS · provideocoalition.com

AI and VFX costs

A cinematographer is publicly saying AI could cut VFX costs on big productions. It is one voice, not a trend, but clients may hear it. Expect questions on where machine learning can replace outsourced clean-up work.

  • Matthew Libatique Says AI Could Cut Marvel’s VFX Costs, but Doubts It Will Use AI Actors · mezha.net Libatique names glare correction as machine learning work that could replace cheap offshore labour, the sort of task you may be asked to reprice

Franchise money

HBO's Harry Potter series is reported to rank among its most expensive, per early estimates. If so, it may mean sustained creature, environment and virtual production work, with vendors competing early for key sequences.

  • HBO prepares a Harry Potter series with a record budget · foro3d.com A reportedly record-level series budget suggests creature and environment work, and early positioning for sequences may matter for bidding

items.title: #19: Breakdown reels show who wins lead-vendor work, while USD and incentives shift the ground
items.summary: Lead-vendor wins on big and mid-size shows set the benchmark you bid against, and some now openly use generative AI.
items.content_html:
Lead-vendor wins on big and mid-size shows set the benchmark you bid against, and some now openly use generative AI. Standards work on USD and a shaky freelance picture in the UK and California are the context to watch when pricing and staffing.

Shot breakdowns and show credits

Reels show who holds lead-vendor slots and at what scale: a 418-shot lead at one end, sole-vendor 300 to 380 shot packages at the other. Useful for calibrating your own bids. The BOT VFX note on generative AI beside CG suggests AI is entering delivered work.

  • Digital Domain Breaks Down 418 VFX Shots for Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day' · awn.com Sets a scale marker: a lead vendor with nearly 400 artists, plus a new creature muscle system that may raise the bar on creature bids
  • Lugundtrug breaks down the VFX of Der Medicus II with more than 380 shots · foro3d.com A German studio as sole VFX provider on 380-plus shots shows what a single European vendor can take on, relevant to Nordic and European competition
  • Young Washington: BOT VFX Recreates 18th-Century America with Invisible Effects · artofvfx.com BOT VFX credits generative AI alongside CG on 300-plus shots, a sign AI use is being openly stated in delivered work
  • Framestore Revisits the CG Joey and 300-Strong Cavalry of 'War Horse' · Animation World Network Mostly clean-up and replication rather than hero creature work, a reminder that much of a bid is invisible fixes, and that is worth pricing

Update: virtual production in Europe

Update: the new piece looks at Europe-wide LED stage growth, with Nordic pop-up stage use named. It also flags readiness gaps among smaller companies, which may limit VP demand and shape what clients ask you to quote.

  • Beyond the backlot: Reinventing drama in the age of virtual production · nordiskfilmogtvfond.com Nordic VP use is real but skills and cost barriers remain, so expect uneven client demand and tight planning requirements

USD standards in the pipeline

An open test bed is exposing where USD handling differs between tools, including renderers lighting the same asset differently. If you run or plan a USD pipeline, this is free validation material and an early warning on interchange problems with partner vendors.

  • Academy Software Foundation’s USD Working Group Launches USD Collaborative Projects Initiative · aswf.io Worth pulling into your own pipeline tests before relying on USD for cross-vendor asset handover

Update: incentives and freelance labour

Update: California is discussing lifting or removing its cap, though lawmakers call it a heavy lift. The UK Budget disappointed the freelancer union over tax timing. Both bear on where work goes and on freelancer cashflow and rates.

  • UK Budget ‘missed opportunity’ to help freelancers claims Bectu chief Childs · c21media.net Earlier tax payments could squeeze UK freelancers' cashflow, which may feed into rate demands if you hire from the UK

items.title: #18: AI is moving into Nuke and Resolve, so bid for new workflows
items.summary: Both main finishing tools now plug into AI assistants, which may shift how you scope compositing and post hours.
items.content_html:
Both main finishing tools now plug into AI assistants, which may shift how you scope compositing and post hours. Meanwhile UK studio money keeps flowing, and cross-border vendor ties are winning real shot counts. Worth checking pipeline assumptions before the next bid.

Studios and incentives

UK public money is backing new stage space outside London. More capacity could ease competition for stages and may widen where UK-based productions shoot, which matters if you bid against or alongside British vendors. The NSI lab headline hints at similar training investment elsewhere, but there is no detail to act on.

  • UK Budget promises £20 million for ‘Hollywood of the North’ · tvbeurope.com Two new sound stages in Liverpool, backed by £20 million, may add UK capacity and regional competition for shows you pitch for
  • NSI launches AI, virtual production lab in Manitoba · playbackonline.ca A Canadian AI and virtual production lab is a sign of public money going into these skills, though the headline alone gives no detail

AI in pipelines

Nuke and Resolve are both gaining AI hooks. Generative elements inside the comp graph and assistant-driven automation in post could trim routine hours, so your bids may need to say where AI is allowed and how it is priced. Nuke 18.0 is only in beta, so treat it as something to test.

  • Foundry releases Nuke 18.0 in open beta · cgchannel.com A Griptape node in Nuke lets compositors generate elements in the node graph, which may change how you scope cleanup and element work
  • How AI assistants are speeding up post production · tvbeurope.com Resolve's assistant support automates metadata, versioning and batch tasks, which suggests lower post hours for repetitive work, worth testing before pricing

Notable shows and credits

Invisible work like environment extensions and small digital fixes is a steady source of work on series. Seeing how a vendor presents it shows what producers value in a showreel for this kind of job.

  • Lanterns: Discover CoSA VFX’s Invisible Effects, From Digital Landscapes to a Beard · artofvfx.com CoSA VFX's Lanterns work shows subtle environment extension is credited work worth pitching, and who to watch for similar series bids

Vendor partnerships

An Indian studio won 300 shots on a feature through a regional producer relationship built on trust. It suggests overflow work can go to well-connected partners, which is worth knowing when you weigh outsourcing or compete with it.

  • Beyond the Render: Craft, Hospitality and the Human side of Cross-Border VFX, LBB · lbbonline.com Resonance landing 300 shots on Land of Bad via a regional bridge shows the kind of offshore competition you may face on bids

items.title: #17: French VFX pay and AI rules are contested, while ILM spreads work across three sites
items.summary: French animation and VFX workers are pressing on pay, job titles and generative AI rules, which could shape costs and contract terms on shared European bids.
items.content_html:
French animation and VFX workers are pressing on pay, job titles and generative AI rules, which could shape costs and contract terms on shared European bids. Show breakdowns also show who is winning work and how it is split across sites. Worth watching: the 18 November walkout.

Labour action in France

The SNTPCT union has called a two-hour walkout of French animation and VFX workers, which could signal rising labour tension in the sector and is worth watching. If employers concede, French cost bases and AI clauses may shift. Worth watching for anyone pricing co-productions or subcontracting to French studios.

  • SNTPCT Calls for 2-Hour Walkout of French Animation and VFX Workers · Animation World Network Pay, job-title and AI demands could raise French labour costs and set a template for AI consent and credit clauses in bids

Pipeline tools

A Foundry video covers Katana, Nuke and USD use on Toy Story 5. It is a pointer to how a large studio builds its pipeline around USD.

  • New Foundry video looks at use of Katana, Nuke, and USD by Pixar in ‘Toy Story 5’ · befores & afters

ILM's dinosaur work

ILM delivered around 700 shots across Sydney, San Francisco and Vancouver, with environments in Sydney and previs, postvis and creatures elsewhere. That split suggests how large work is divided by site specialism. Useful reference when pitching environment-heavy or creature-heavy packages.

  • ILM Builds 700 Shots of Prehistoric Suburbia for 'The End of Oak Street' · Animation World Network Shows a clear site-by-discipline split on a 700-shot job, a model for structuring multi-site bids
  • ILM BRINGS DINOSAURS TO SUBURBIA FOR THE END OF OAK STREET · vfxvoice.com Production VFX supervisor Jay Cooper describes creature design freedom and digital geography fixes, useful for scoping similar creature and environment work

Who did the work on recent shows

Union VFX took 234 shots on a mid-scale A24 and StudioCanal film, mostly environments, set extensions and practical-plus-digital effects. Both help gauge where mid-size studios compete.

  • Union VFX Delivers 234 Shots for Glen Powell's 'How to Make a Killing' · awn.com A mid-size studio winning 234 shots of environment and effects work shows the kind of package open to smaller houses
  • Resident Evil: Alessandro Ongaro – Production VFX Supervisor · artofvfx.com

items.title: #10: Proof expands into New York while Netflix cuts staff: watch where visualisation work lands
items.summary: A visualisation house is adding a permanent East Coast base while the streamer trims headcount. Buyer-side cost pressure may reach vendor budgets and bids.
items.content_html:
A visualisation house is adding a permanent East Coast base while the streamer trims headcount. Buyer-side cost pressure may reach vendor budgets and bids. Worth watching whether Proof's expansion pulls previs work away from European shops.

Studio openings and buyer cuts

Proof is growing its footprint in a new market, which suggests more competition for previs and virtual production bids tied to US directors. Netflix's cuts hit product, tech, legal and HR, not production, but wider layoffs may mean tighter buyer budgets and harder rate talks.

  • Ron Frankel Brings Proof Home to Manhattan with New York Studio · awn.com A permanent Proof base in New York, with Ari Aster's next feature as first project, adds a rival for visualisation bids on US-led projects
  • Netflix lays off 6% of workforce in streamer’s biggest cull · screendaily.com Update: Netflix is cutting roughly 6% of staff, not in production teams, but it points to cost discipline that may reach vendor budgets

Pipeline and production work

Framestore's creature work on a returning streaming show is a reference point for how long-running episodic VFX is credited and sold.

  • How Framestore made Appa · befores & afters Framestore is credited with making Appa for season two of Avatar: The Last Airbender, a useful benchmark for episodic creature bids

items.title: #9: Eyeline's AI hybrid work is now on shows; expect it in bid conversations
items.summary: Netflix's in-house studio has moved from AI pitch to credited shows, and Netflix is reportedly cutting staff.
items.content_html:
Netflix's in-house studio has moved from AI pitch to credited shows, and Netflix is reportedly cutting staff. Clients may push harder on price for crowds and set extensions. Worth watching how your bids frame hybrid work, and which shots you keep traditional.

AI tools aimed at control and dialogue changes

Both items pitch AI as something that keeps human-made inputs in charge: 3D data guiding generation, and original performances preserved in lipsync. That may shift some cleanup and localisation work to managed services. Worth checking what your pipeline offers around consistency and ownership.

  • Reallusion and Escape.AI Partner to Solve AI Video Bottlenecks and Expand Distribution · befores & afters A 3D-guided AI route could compete with small-scale animation bids, and its focus on provable authorship may matter to clients
  • Sync.Labs Intros Zero-Shot Lipsyncing for Film and Television · postperspective.com Post-shoot line changes and localisation fixes are work VFX houses sometimes bid on, and a managed service is now on offer

Netflix cuts and a tax-cap warning

Netflix is reportedly trimming about 5% of staff while keeping a content budget of around $20 billion, so spend may hold even as in-house teams shrink. The Australian rebate dispute shows how incentive uncertainty can push productions elsewhere, so check any incentive assumptions in your own bids.

  • Netflix Reportedly Trimming 5% of Staff as Growth Slows · awn.com Reported cuts may affect who you deal with at Netflix, though the stated content budget suggests work may continue
  • Australian producers step up calls for removal of 20% cap on key tax rebate · screendaily.com One producer is weighing a move to New Zealand over the cap, a sign that incentive uncertainty can move projects

Who did what: crowds, extensions and miniatures

Crowd and environment extension are standard bid line items, and they show up across these credits. The Laika numbers are a useful scale reference for how a practical-heavy show gets planned and staffed.

  • Watch beloFX’s VFX breakdown for Mother Mary · cgchannel.com A 156-shot count with CG stadium crowds and cloth sim gives a reference point for mid-sized scope and a competitor's positioning
  • The Dog Stars: Stuart Bullen (VFX Supervisor) and Michelle Cullen (VFX Producer) – RISE · artofvfx.com RISE's runway, vegetation and crowd replication work shows the kind of set-extension scope a studio can win on a practical shoot
  • Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ VFX Supervisor Steve Emerson Details the Making of Travis Knight’s Stop-Motion Epic · variety.com Shot counts nearly double the studio's earlier film show how fast scope grows, which matters for schedule and bid risk

items.title: #8: UK vendors keep spreading regionally while ML face work earns Emmy-level recognition
items.summary: Mid-size UK studios are adding regional bases, which means more competition for bids close to your market.
items.content_html:
Mid-size UK studios are adding regional bases, which means more competition for bids close to your market. Meanwhile, ML face replacement has moved from novelty to recognised production tool. Worth checking where both sit in your next pitch.

Capacity and competition, ML in the pipeline

Vine FX is widening its UK footprint, which may sharpen competition for co-production and service work that Copenhagen shops also chase. Separately, an Emmy for ML face replacement suggests clients will increasingly expect it as a priced line item. Worth watching how consent and licensing terms get written into bids.

  • Vine FX Continues UK Expansion with Cardiff Studio Opening · ukscreenalliance.co.uk A third UK base with a pipeline through 2026 suggests a larger rival for shows where UK and Nordic vendors compete
  • Making history with AI · tvbeurope.com Emmy recognition makes ML face work a credible bid option, with consent-trained and deleted-after-project models set as the benchmark clients may ask about

items.title: #7: A new studio landing a horror feature shows where mid-size work is going
items.summary: Roxel Creative founder Calvin Romeyn serving as associate VFX supervisor on Backrooms, the studio's first major project, could be a useful signal for anyone
items.content_html:
Roxel Creative founder Calvin Romeyn serving as associate VFX supervisor on Backrooms, the studio's first major project, could be a useful signal for anyone bidding mid-size work.

Small studios taking on feature-scale work

Roxel Creative's first major project was the feature Backrooms, where founder Calvin Romeyn also served as associate VFX supervisor on the entire movie, suggesting a strong debut for the studio. That suggests newer, leaner studios can compete for sizeable scope. Worth watching as a possible partner or rival on future bids, especially for CG environment extensions of practical sets.

  • Check out Roxel Creative’s eerie VFX breakdown for Backrooms · cgchannel.com Roxel Creative, founded by Calvin Romeyn, worked on Backrooms with Romeyn as associate VFX supervisor, which suggests small, newly formed studios could turn up as rivals or vendor partners on bids.
  • Creating the Spinosaurus for ‘The End of Oak Street’ · befores & afters

items.title: #6: Incentives pull post work abroad while Netflix pushes AI into pipelines
items.summary: Two items today: an Australian studio shows how rebates and time zones win US post work, and Netflix details how widely it now uses AI in production.
items.content_html:
Two items today: an Australian studio shows how rebates and time zones win US post work, and Netflix details how widely it now uses AI in production.

Incentives and time zones shape where post goes

KOJO credits a rebate of up to 45 per cent, a favourable exchange rate and overnight turnaround for lifting US work. Expect Copenhagen bids to be compared against that kind of package, especially on shows shot elsewhere and finished abroad.

  • KOJO Celebrates 30 Years as US Demand Drives Australian Post-Production Growth · filmink.com.au US demand is growing Australian post-production work

AI moves into mainstream production workflows

Netflix says AI is in use across around 300 titles, including previs and VFX, and Eyeline used generative tools for crowds on one title. Clients may start asking for hybrid pricing, so work out where generative steps could cut your own crowd and previs lines.

  • Netflix Expands Asia Production Budgets and AI Tools to Tackle Talent Bottlenecks · retailnews.asia

items.title: #5: Netflix says AI touches 300 titles; director claims 40% savings
items.summary: A Busan panel put numbers on AI in production, from a streamer with its own VFX house and a director chasing lower budgets.
items.content_html:
A Busan panel put numbers on AI in production, from a streamer with its own VFX house and a director chasing lower budgets.

Netflix puts AI across the pipeline

Netflix names previs, design, editorial and VFX as AI use cases, and Eyeline pushes a hybrid of live action, VFX and generative tools. Expect clients to ask which shots can go that route, and to question bids for crowd and creature work.

  • AI Can Cut Film Budgets by Up to 40%, Says ‘The Outlaws’ Director Kang Yoon-sung, as Netflix Reveals Use on 300 Titles: ‘A Human Touch Is Absolutely Essential’ · variety.com
  • Netflix Executive Says AI Has Touched 300 Titles as Director Claims Budget Savings of Up to 40% · northeasttimes.com Netflix AI use on 300 titles; budget impact

Budget claims and the human check

Still, the same panel stressed human judgement on emotion, so position supervision and artist finishing as the quality guarantee in bids.

  • Generative AI Still Needs Artists’ Judgment, Says Netflix’s Eyeline GenFX Chief James Rustad at Busan · imdb.com

items.title: #3: Outpost lands in Germany as Europe's VFX map shifts
items.summary: One European studio expansion today, plus two breakdowns showing how far environment work is being pushed on post-apocalyptic shows.
items.content_html:
One European studio expansion today, plus two breakdowns showing how far environment work is being pushed on post-apocalyptic shows.

Studio expansion into Europe

Outpost now offers a German base with access to regional and federal incentives, plus a senior creature team. Expect it to compete for the same European episodic work, and possibly undercut on incentive-led pricing.

  • Outpost VFX Opens in Germany, Taps 'House of the Dragon' Vet Sven Martin · awn.com

Environment work on post-apocalyptic shows

Both breakdowns lean on large 3D city builds over matte painting, with BlueBolt using hundreds of assets and Framestore painting only the focal points. Useful reference when scoping wide-shot environments: asset counts and camera freedom drive cost, and selective detail keeps it down.

  • Watch BlueBolt’s VFX breakdown for The Dog Stars · cgchannel.com
  • VFX Breakdown: NYC in The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 · 80.lv

items.title: #1: Studio capacity grows while European VFX economics tighten
items.summary: New stages and virtual production assets are changing hands across Europe and beyond, while one UK post house has gone through pre-pack administration.
items.content_html:
New stages and virtual production assets are changing hands across Europe and beyond, while one UK post house has gone through pre-pack administration.

Studio capacity and virtual production moves

More stage and post capacity in the UK and Poland means more rival locations competing for the same productions, so check where your bids sit on cost and facilities. The Pixomondo virtual production asset sale shows how quickly that infrastructure gets reshuffled.

  • Sunderland’s Crown Works Studios wins planning permission for first phase · ibc.org
  • Playhouse Post opens revamped Noel Street facility · televisual.com
  • ETC adds studio in Poland · televisual.com
  • Dark Slope Acquires Pixomondo's Virtual Production Assets · awn.com
  • LensStory Opens Melbourne Virtual Production Studio · content-technology.com
  • Hollywood River Studios Breaks Ground On Major Production St. Louis Campus · tvtechnology.com

Economics, tax and talent in Europe

The ELMNTL administration is a reminder that thin margins can sink a facility mid-project, so vet partners and vendors carefully before subcontracting. The European tax, talent and cost pieces are useful benchmarks when pricing against rivals.

  • ELMNTL joins Alongside after pre-pack administration · televisual.com
  • VFX IN EUROPE: NAVIGATING TALENT, TAX, TECHNOLOGY AND TURBULENCE · vfxvoice.com
  • ACCOUNTING FOR THE NEW ECONOMICS OF VFX · vfxvoice.com
  • Lucky Luciano Becomes Global Production Network’s Exclusive Partner in Poland, LBB · lbbonline.com

Tools and who is winning the work

Mocap and new tooling are shifting what virtual production pipelines can do, which feeds into schedules and quotes. The Rodeo FX and Koala FX breakdowns show who is landing the work and what they deliver on it.

  • THE TOOLS SHAPING THE FUTURE OF VFX · vfxvoice.com
  • Use Cases for Motion Capture for Virtual Production · vfxvoice.com
  • Rodeo FX’s ‘House of the Dragon’ s3 VFX breakdown is here · befores & afters
  • ‘Fall 2’ reaches new heights in VFX · befores & afters
